summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable sticky directory and verified it persists across reboot.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop with root:root ownership and mode 1777.
Verified distinct non-root users can write and delete their own files but cannot delete files owned by another user.
Safely rebooted node1, confirmed its boot identity changed, and verified directory permissions and behavior recovered.
Removed temporary verification files; /srv/drop is empty.

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop is shared writable and prevents cross-user deletion
evidence.summary: Mode is 1777 (drwxrwxrwt); two non-root identities wrote successfully, own-file deletion succeeded, and cross-user deletion failed with Operation not permitted.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 984a7d52-3387-4830-a06e-15e8b5e6c2a1, safe reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 202fa7f7-2243-4342-8fea-a991898ab617, running system state, persisted data, mode 1777, shared writes, and sticky-bit protection after restart.
